- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75–80 range), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture the “rebound” or “mean reversion” phase.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the final 10–15 days of the forecast horizon, often underestimating true price drops.
- Model reacts too slowly to recent price declines — fails to “catch up” with true trend shifts, especially after 20–30 days of downward momentum.
- Forecasts show strong persistence of recent highs, failing to adjust for seasonal or policy-driven mean reversion (e.g., post-peak price corrections).
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 5–10 days, especially when true prices show sudden drops or erratic behavior.
- Model tends to “smooth” sharp price reversals — fails to recognize short-term volatility spikes or sudden policy interventions.
